candidates.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
candidates.summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. candidates.title: Resolving “that thing” — and what belongs inside a factory
candidates.summary:
One of the most common references in long-running work is “that thing.”

“The file from Tuesday.” “The bridge we made.” “That account.”

A model can guess. It can ask. Or it can derive the answer from what actually exists.

There’s a method for this, and it composes with whatever other factories and derivations you already have going.
